content.value_statement: React teams can hit stale state, render timing, and async action bugs when using Zustand. This skill gives direct patterns for stores, selectors, derived state, testing, debugging, and persistence.
actual_capabilities: Explains why Zustand set updates synchronously while React renders later.
Shows how get and getState avoid stale closures after async work.
Compares selector patterns that reduce unnecessary React re-renders.
Describes derived state, subscriptions, testing resets, debugging, and persistence.
Includes migration notes for Zustand 4.x and 5.x shallow selector APIs.
limitations: It is documentation only and does not inspect a project automatically.
It does not generate a full application architecture by itself.
It assumes users already use React or React Native with Zustand.
It does not cover every Zustand middleware or ecosystem package.

use_cases.title: Debug stale React state
use_cases.description: Use the timing patterns to explain why store values update before components re-render.

use_cases.title: Design async store actions
use_cases.description: Use the async action guidance to make loading, data, and error state easier to reason about.

use_cases.title: Review Zustand migrations
use_cases.description: Use the selector and migration notes when moving stores from Zustand 4.x to 5.x.

prompt_templates.title: Explain store timing
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner review of Zustand update behavior.
prompt_templates.prompt: Explain why my React component still shows old Zustand state after I call set. Keep the explanation practical.

prompt_templates.title: Fix stale closures
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this Zustand action for stale closure problems after await. Suggest where get or getState should be used.

prompt_templates.title: Improve selectors
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my Zustand selectors for unnecessary re-renders. Recommend multiple selectors, shallow comparison, or useShallow where appropriate.

prompt_templates.title: Audit store architecture
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced review across actions, persistence, and tests.
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit this Zustand store design for async races, derived state, selector stability, persistence boundaries, and test reset strategy.

output_examples.input: A component reads a count value immediately after an increment action.
output_examples.output: The answer explains store state updates immediately, while the component view changes after React completes its next render.

output_examples.input: An async action reads captured data after a delayed save operation.
output_examples.output: The answer recommends reading current store data after the delay, then updating state from that current value.

output_examples.input: A selector returns a new object on every render.
output_examples.output: The answer explains why this can cause extra renders and suggests stable selector patterns for the installed Zustand version.

best_practices: Read current store state after await when correctness depends on fresh values.
Keep derived values in selectors unless storing them avoids real repeated work.
Reset store state explicitly in tests before each case.
anti_patterns: Do not assume a React component has re-rendered immediately after a store update.
Do not return fresh selector objects without shallow comparison or useShallow.
Do not persist an entire store when only a small state slice is needed.

faq.question: Does this skill execute code?
faq.answer: No. It provides guidance and examples for Zustand usage.

faq.question: Does it support React Native?
faq.answer: Yes. The core Zustand patterns apply to React web and React Native.

faq.question: Can it help with Zustand 5.x?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes notes about shallow selector changes in Zustand 5.x.

faq.question: Can it debug stale state bugs?
faq.answer: Yes. It explains render timing, closures, and current state reads.

faq.question: Does it replace Zustand documentation?
faq.answer: No. It focuses on common patterns and pitfalls, not every API detail.

faq.question: Is it useful for tests?
faq.answer: Yes. It describes reset patterns and async store assertions.
